- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes in price (e.g., 35.63 → 36.62, 35.44 → 38.18).
- Underestimates when prices dip below 34.00, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Shows persistent lag in recognizing true price peaks; forecasts peak prices too early or too low.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 35.63 → 36.62, 34.08 → 38.18) and fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts too long after peaks.
- Forecasts tend to be overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, underreacting to sustained high prices.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior around 34.00–35.00 range, failing to adjust to true volatility beyond that band.
- Overconfidence in short-term trends; fails to account for macroeconomic or policy-driven corrections (e.g., EU ETS cap adjustments).
